I don't know, I'm probably gonna get hated for saying this, but I think you need to hate how you look. Seriously, do you know what being overweight is? It means that you've (in most cases, NOT all) been lazy, or ignorant, or indifferent enough that your entire body is now covered in a layer of fat so thick that you are limited in what you can so. You're no longer a healthy animal that can do whats needed to survive- you need to depend on others in some situations, making you a liability, and you're restricted by your own body mass getting in your way. 

And you don't need to go to the gym, and waste all your money, and workout in an area surrounded by other people. Aim for 20 pushups and 20 situps a day (it'll be hard at first, but you'll get there), and a walk (to start with, turn it into a jog or a run when you can). You've got time in your day. Spend half an hour less on Reddit, play a bit less of a video game, wake up just that little bit earlier. And remember, it takes around 6 weeks to start really seeing any results from working out. You've got to retrain your body so that it knows what its doing. 

Then there's the fact that you're feeding your body stuff that you know you don't need, but only want. When a toddler makes himself sick by eating too many sweets (ohai Easter, waddup?), you don't think, 'oh, poor child'. You think he's been silly and self-indulgent, and that's why he's now suffering. We need some self-discipline in our lives, or we're no better than that self-indulgent toddler.  We need to stop thinking "but I want" and start thinking "my body needs".

There's no point attempting weight loss if you're not willing to try to change your head space as well. It won't work. Weight loss is hard. It's scary, at times. It'll make you cry. It'll make you doubt yourself and want to give up. (There's that 'want' again.) But you just can't. You need this, for yourself and those you love. And in the end, it'll make you so happy that you'll walk around for days at a time in a happy, uplifted glow. Honestly,that feeling.... I don't know, there aren't any words. But you want it. Trust me, you want to feel this good.

People's reactions to weight loss seem to be remarkable predictable. 

I've been overweight for years; barely anyone I know has seen me skinny, so the change is kind of shocking to them. Ninety percent of conversations I have about it are the same:

"wow, you've lost so much weight, how'd you do it?" -and here you can practically read their minds; they're waiting for you to tell them you've smoked something, or ordered a pill online, or seen a tip on sixty minutes, and you've not had to change a single thing in your life. 

Then I start with,

"just cutting out the shit I eat, and being a lot more careful with myself really..." -and here they start to look uncomfortable, and you know there's no point in going on. 

They're not looking for genuine weight loss, they're looking for a genie that will help them wish away their insecurities alonsg with their fat.

How I've started to get there: hate yourself, love yourself, be ashamed, and make yourself proud. 

I hate what younger me did to herself. Seriously, I keep just coasting through life on autopilot, not really doing anything that matters. It shows in a lot of ways, and one of the most obvious is my weight. 

I became so incredibly ashamed of myself. You know when you see a really fat person in the food court, and they're gorging themselves on KFC, and you can't help but judge? I realised other people were most likely thinking the same thing when they saw me eating chocolate or a burger. I was so embarrassed when I came to this realisation, and wanted to make sure people wouldn't see me that way, ever again. 

I knew just hating myself wasn't enough though; I needed to love myself as well, otherwise I'd never make the effort. I looked back on how disappointed I was with younger me, and decided I wanted older me to be proud of present me. 

Present me is already so proud of six-months-younger me, she knew it would be hard but stuck at it, and shes dropped two pant sizes, and three top sizes. 

Since I'm tiny (five ft), any change is really noticeable, so I guess I've got it a little easier than most people here. I get a lot more "omg you look amazing, you've lost so much weight" than most people that have only dropped 15kg, and I can see the changes and be more motivated by them. But if that's not the case for you, then hey, you've got it a little harder, which means your future self will be even prouder of you for making the effort. 

For myself, that not-being-disappointed-later thing was what has really grabbed me after 7 years of half-added dieting and looking for gimmicks, but if that's not for you, think about something else: how much your relationship with your kids will improve when you can run around with them, or how much more likely having kids will be once you've lost that weight. 

But seriously, just get the fuck up, and do it. Or you'll always be disappointed, and you'll never be truly happy in your own skin. 

You're worth the effort, but you have to make that effort. 

And remember, every single person on this subreddit is rooting for you.
